Hi Connor,

Thanks for the quick signup — attaching our VAT cert and a sample invoice so your team can confirm routing. A couple of points we need clarified before we complete setup:

- Atlas is VAT-registered in DE (USt-IdNr DE123456789). We issue invoices net with reverse-charge when the buyer is an EU business.
- For POs: our finance team prefers POs to be created to the German entity (Atlas Logistics GmbH) but routed to the EU-payments queue if reverse-charge applies.
- Any onboarding form / tax attestation you need, we can fill it out and return.

Hi Anna — thanks for the documents, received. I looped in Laura (payments) and Karthik (tax ops) so we can confirm exact PO flags. Quick intake so we handle this correctly in the vendor record: 

1) Legal vendor name to show on PO/invoice: Atlas Logistics GmbH
2) Country of tax domicile: Germany
3) VAT ID: DE123456789 (you included cert — thanks)
4) Do you ever bill us with VAT charged (B2B to non-EU customers) or is it always net with reverse-charge for Redwood?

Next steps from our side once we confirm the answers: create the vendor profile, set the tax domicile and VAT ID, and set an automated PO-routing rule that flips the invoice queue to EU-payments when the vendor's tax_domicile == EU and reverse_charge == true. Karthik — can you advise on the decision-tree node logic we should codify?

Connor O'Brien

Hi Connor,

Answers below:
- Legal name on PO/invoice: Atlas Logistics GmbH
- Tax domicile: Germany (legal entity taxed in DE)
- VAT ID: DE123456789 (attached certificate)
- Billing behavior: for Redwood (EU business) we issue net invoices and include the line "reverse charge - VAT due by customer". We only charge VAT on B2C sales or where the buyer is outside the EU and local rules require it.

We can complete any onboarding form you send. Also happy to connect if you want to walk through a sample PO/invoice mapping.

Regards,
Anna

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 07:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: supplier tax domicile decision tree & PO automation

Connor / Laura — drafted the decision-tree nodes we should implement in vendor intake and PO routing. Summary (high level):

1) Vendor tax_domicile == EU && has_valid_vat_id == true -> set vendor.tax_rule = "reverse_charge_possible"
   - PO flag: reverse_charge_allowed = true
   - Routing: invoices -> EU-payments queue (for net invoiced B2B)

2) Vendor tax_domicile == non-EU && supplies services from outside EU -> standard VAT treatment; tag vendor as "non_eu_supplier"

3) If vendor provides mixed supply (goods + services) -> require granularity on invoice lines; default to manual review by finance if VAT_collected == ambiguous

Operational notes:
- We should store tax_proof_doc link in vendor record (attestation field) and surface in PO creation UI.
- Add an audit note for any override of the reverse_charge flag; overrides must be approved by Finance (Laura).
- For automation: implement a lightweight rule engine that evaluates vendor.tax_domicile, vendor.vat_id_presence, and invoice.indicator_reverse_charge. If all three align, set invoice.processing_queue = "eu-payments".

I've attached a simple SVG decision-tree (decision-tree-v1.svg) to iterate on. Connor — once we confirm, I can hand this to infra for the routing rule.

Thanks,
Karthik
Tax Operations Manager

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>

Operational notes for Atlas: please confirm the preferred PO billing entity (you indicated Atlas Logistics GmbH) and whether your team wants POs created with a note "reverse charge applies" so your AP team can match without manual steps.

I'll send the onboarding form and a vendor-portal invite link once the vendor record is created: https://app.redwood.internal/vendor/atlas-logistics

Best regards,
